title: Telling a story
goal: Tell a story about your past: set the scene, describe what you used to do, and say what happened.

grammar.p: The imperfect is the second past tense. It is very regular. -ar verbs: *-aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban* (*caminaba*). -er and -ir verbs: *-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían* (*comía, vivía*). Only three verbs are irregular: *ser → era, eras, era, éramos, eran*; *ir → iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban*; *ver → veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían*. The yo and él/ella/usted forms are the same (*yo trabajaba / ella trabajaba*), so use a subject or context when needed. The past of *hay* for a description is *había* (there was / there were).
ex: Mi papá trabajaba en una fábrica.
My dad worked in a factory.
Íbamos a la playa todos los veranos.
We used to go to the beach every summer.
En mi pueblo había una sola escuela.
In my town there was only one school.

grammar.p: Use the imperfect for what you used to do, or did again and again with no clear end: *de niño*, *cuando era joven*, *antes*, *siempre*, *a veces*, *todos los días*, *cada verano*, *los domingos*. Use the preterite for one specific event or a closed block of time: *ayer*, *una vez*, *el lunes pasado*, *por cinco años*. Compare: *De niño jugaba béisbol* (I used to play) vs. *Ayer jugué béisbol* (I played, once). Note: a finished length of time takes the preterite: *Viví en México cinco años* (I lived in Mexico for five years).
ex: De niño, jugaba béisbol todos los días.
As a kid, I played baseball every day.
Antes fumaba, pero lo dejé.
I used to smoke, but I quit.
Viví en Monterrey cinco años.
I lived in Monterrey for five years.

grammar.p: In a story, the imperfect paints the scene: what was going on, the time, age, weather, how people felt. The preterite moves the story forward: what happened. A very common pattern is an action in progress (imperfect) interrupted by an event (preterite): *Yo estaba en la ducha cuando sonó el teléfono*. *Mientras* (while) usually introduces the background action in the imperfect. Time and age are always imperfect: *Eran las diez*, *Tenía ocho años*. *De repente* (suddenly) signals an event in the preterite.
ex: Eran las tres de la mañana cuando me llamaron del hospital.
It was three in the morning when they called me from the hospital.
Mientras cocinaba, llegó mi hijo.
While I was cooking, my son got home.
Llovía y hacía frío. De repente, se fue la luz.
It was raining and it was cold. Suddenly, the power went out.

grammar.h: Verbs that change meaning in the preterite
grammar.p: Four verbs mean something different in the preterite because the preterite marks a moment. *conocer*: *conocía* = I knew (someone) / *conocí* = I met (for the first time). *saber*: *sabía* = I knew / *supe* = I found out. *querer*: *quería* = I wanted / *quise* = I tried; *no quise* = I refused. *poder*: *podía* = I was able to (in general) / *pude* = I managed to; *no pude* = I tried and failed.
ex: Conocí a mi esposa en una boda.
I met my wife at a wedding.
No sabía que hablabas español.
I didn't know you spoke Spanish.
Anoche supe la verdad.
Last night I found out the truth.
Mi hija no quiso comer.
My daughter refused to eat.
Por fin pude dormir.
I finally managed to sleep.

vocab: to meet for the first time
phrases: When I was ten years old…
As a kid, I lived in…
We always used to go to…
Where did you live when you were a kid?
How did you meet your wife?
What did you use to do? (polite)
Eran como las diez de la noche.
It was around ten at night.
I tried to call, but I couldn't.

items.q: De niño, yo ___ al parque todos los días.
items.qen: As a kid, I used to go to the park every day.
items.why: A habit in childhood (de niño, todos los días) → imperfect of ir: iba.

items.q: Cuando yo ___ niño, vivíamos en Puebla.
items.qen: When I was a kid, we lived in Puebla.
items.why: Age/stage of life is background → imperfect of ser: era. 'Cuando fui niño' is not used.

items.q: Yo ___ en la ducha cuando sonó el teléfono.
items.qen: I was in the shower when the phone rang.
items.why: The situation already in progress when something happened → imperfect: estaba.

items.q: Yo estaba en la ducha cuando de repente ___ el teléfono.
items.qen: I was in the shower when suddenly the phone rang.
items.why: The interrupting event (de repente) → preterite: sonó. Sonaron is plural; el teléfono is singular.

items.q: ___ las once de la noche cuando llegamos a casa.
items.qen: It was eleven at night when we got home.
items.why: Clock time in the past is always imperfect, and plural for las once → eran. Era is only for la una.

items.q: Ayer yo ___ a la nueva enfermera del piso.
items.qen: Yesterday I met the new nurse on the floor.
items.why: Meeting someone for the first time, at one moment → preterite: conocí.

items.q: Anoche yo ___ que mi primo tuvo un accidente.
items.qen: Last night I found out that my cousin had an accident.
items.why: 'Found out' → preterite of saber: supe. Supo = he/she found out.

items.q: Mientras yo ___, mi hijo llegó a casa.
items.qen: While I was cooking, my son got home.
items.why: Mientras + the background action that was in progress → imperfect: cocinaba.

items.q: In 'Quise abrir la puerta, pero no pude', what does 'quise' mean?
items.why: querer in the preterite = tried. 'No pude' = I tried and failed.

items.q: How do you say 'My daughter refused to eat the vegetables last night'?
opts: Mi hija no quería comer las verduras anoche.
Mi hija no quiso comer las verduras anoche.
Mi hija no quiere comer las verduras anoche.
Mi hija no quise comer las verduras anoche.
items.why: 'Refused' → no + preterite of querer: no quiso. No quería = she didn't feel like it (a feeling, not a refusal).

items.q: Antes yo ___, pero lo dejé hace cinco años.
items.qen: I used to smoke, but I quit five years ago.
items.why: 'Used to' (a past habit, with antes) → imperfect: fumaba.

items.q: How do you say 'We used to see my grandparents every Sunday'?
opts: Vimos a mis abuelos todos los domingos.
Vemos a mis abuelos todos los domingos.
Veían a mis abuelos todos los domingos.
Veíamos a mis abuelos todos los domingos.
items.why: 'Used to' → imperfect; nosotros of ver → veíamos (with an accent).

items.q: Cuando ___ diez años, me rompí el brazo.
items.qen: When I was ten, I broke my arm.
items.why: Age in the past is background → imperfect: tenía.

items.q: Cuando tenía diez años, ___ el brazo.
items.qen: When I was ten, I broke my arm.
items.why: Breaking your arm is a one-time event → preterite: me rompí. Me rompía would mean it kept happening.

items.q: Cuando yo era niño, mi abuela siempre ___ café de olla en las mañanas.
items.qen: When I was a kid, my grandmother always made café de olla in the mornings.
items.why: A repeated habit (siempre, en las mañanas, 'used to') → imperfect: hacía.

items.q: Choose the sentence that means 'I already knew Ana when she started working here.'
opts: Ya conocí a Ana cuando empezó a trabajar aquí.
Ya conocía a Ana cuando empezó a trabajar aquí.
Ya conozco a Ana cuando empezó a trabajar aquí.
Ya conoció a Ana cuando empezó a trabajar aquí.
items.why: Already knowing someone is an ongoing state → conocía. Conocí would mean 'I met'; conoció is he/she.

items.q: Ayer por fin yo ___ hablar con mi hermano.
items.qen: Yesterday I finally managed to talk to my brother.
items.why: 'Managed to' at one moment → preterite of poder: pude.

items.q: De niños, todos los veranos nosotros ___ a la playa.
items.qen: As kids, every summer we used to go to the beach.
items.why: A repeated habit ('used to', todos los veranos) → imperfect of ir, nosotros: íbamos.

items.q: Cuando yo era niño, la casa de mis abuelos ___ un patio con muchos árboles.
items.qen: When I was a kid, my grandparents' house had a patio with lots of trees.
items.why: Describing how something was → imperfect: tenía.

items.q: How do you say 'Last night I was reading when the power went out'?
opts: Anoche leía cuando se fue la luz.
Anoche leí cuando se iba la luz.
Anoche leía cuando se iba la luz.
Anoche leí cuando se fue la luz.
items.why: Action in progress → imperfect (leía); the interrupting event → preterite (se fue la luz).

items.q: De niño, yo ___ fútbol todos los sábados.
items.en: As a kid, I used to play soccer every Saturday.
items.why: A childhood habit → imperfect: jugaba.

items.q: Cuando yo era niño, mi papá ___ en una fábrica de lunes a sábado.
items.en: When I was a kid, my dad used to work in a factory Monday through Saturday.
items.why: A repeated, ongoing activity in the past ('used to') → imperfect: trabajaba.

items.q: Yo ___ la tele tranquilo cuando de repente llegó mi hermano.
items.en: I was quietly watching TV when suddenly my brother arrived.
items.why: The action in progress when something happened → imperfect of ver: veía (estaba viendo is also correct).

items.q: Anoche, cuando yo ___ a casa a las once, mis hijos ya dormían.
items.en: Last night, when I got home at eleven, my kids were already asleep.
items.why: Getting home is the event (anoche, one time) → preterite: llegué. Dormían is the background.

items.q: ___ las tres de la mañana cuando me llamaron del hospital.
items.en: It was three in the morning when they called me from the hospital.
items.why: Time of day in the past → imperfect, plural for las tres: eran.

items.q: Ayer en la fiesta yo ___ a tu hermano. ¡Qué simpático!
items.en: Yesterday at the party I met your brother. How nice he is!
items.why: Meeting someone for the first time → preterite: conocí.

items.q: Cuando me mudé a Chicago, no ___ a nadie.
items.en: When I moved to Chicago, I didn't know anyone.
items.why: 'Didn't know' anyone is a state → imperfect: conocía.

items.q: El lunes yo ___ que me dieron el trabajo.
items.en: On Monday I found out that I got the job.
items.why: 'Found out' at one moment → preterite of saber: supe.

items.q: Yo no ___ que tu mamá estaba enferma. Lo siento.
items.en: I didn't know your mom was sick. I'm sorry.
items.why: 'Didn't know' is a state → imperfect: sabía.

items.q: Ayer mi hijo no ___ ir a la escuela; lloró toda la mañana.
items.en: Yesterday my son refused to go to school; he cried all morning.
items.why: 'Refused' → no + preterite of querer: no quiso.

items.q: Después de tres horas, por fin ___ dormir.
items.en: After three hours, I finally managed to sleep.
items.why: 'Managed to' at one moment (por fin) → preterite of poder: pude.

items.q: Cuando yo era niño, nosotros ___ a misa todos los domingos.
items.en: When I was a kid, we used to go to Mass every Sunday.
items.why: A habit (todos los domingos, 'used to') → imperfect of ir: íbamos (with an accent).

items.q: De niños, mi hermana y yo siempre ___ caricaturas los sábados en la mañana.
items.en: As kids, my sister and I always used to watch cartoons on Saturday mornings.
items.why: A habit → imperfect of ver, nosotros: veíamos.

items.q: Yo ___ en México cinco años y después me mudé a Chicago.
items.en: I lived in Mexico for five years and then I moved to Chicago.
items.why: A closed block of time (cinco años, then a change) → preterite: viví.

items.q: Cenábamos tranquilos cuando de repente se ___ la luz.
items.en: We were having dinner quietly when suddenly the power went out.
items.why: De repente marks the interrupting event → preterite: se fue la luz.

items.q: Cuando éramos niños, mi abuelo siempre nos ___ cuentos antes de dormir.
items.en: When we were kids, my grandfather always used to tell us stories before bed.
items.why: A repeated habit → imperfect: contaba (no stem change in the imperfect).

items.q: El martes pasado mi mamá ___ a urgencias porque le dolía el pecho.
items.en: Last Tuesday my mom went to the ER because her chest hurt.
items.why: Going to the ER is the event (el martes pasado) → preterite: fue. 'Le dolía' is the background reason.

items.q: La niña ___ ocho años cuando llegó a Chicago.
items.en: The girl was eight years old when she arrived in Chicago.
items.why: Age in the past → imperfect: tenía.

items.q: Mientras yo ___ al trabajo, vi un accidente.
items.en: While I was driving to work, I saw an accident.
items.why: Mientras + the action in progress → imperfect: manejaba (estaba manejando is also correct).

items.q: Cuando mis papás eran jóvenes, nadie ___ celular.
items.en: When my parents were young, nobody had a cell phone.
items.why: Describing how life was back then → imperfect; nadie takes the singular: tenía.

I met my wife at the beach.

turns.en: Hey, where did you live when you were a kid?

opts: Vivía en Ohio con mis papás.
Vivo en Ohio cuando era niño.
turns.why: Where you used to live as a child → imperfect: vivía.

turns.es: ¿Y qué hacías los fines de semana?
turns.en: And what did you do on weekends?

opts: Juego béisbol con mis amigos el año pasado.
turns.why: A weekend habit back then → imperfect, yo: jugaba.

turns.es: ¡Qué padre! Yo jugaba fútbol todos los días después de la escuela.
turns.en: Cool! I used to play soccer every day after school.
Hey, how did you meet your wife?

opts: Conocí a mi esposa en la fiesta de un amigo.
Conocía a mi esposa en la fiesta de un amigo.
Conozco a mi esposa en la fiesta de un amigo.
turns.why: Meeting someone for the first time → preterite: conocí.

turns.es: ¡Qué bonito! ¿Y ya trabajabas aquí en Chicago?
turns.en: How sweet! And were you already working here in Chicago?

opts: No, todavía estudio en la universidad.
No, todavía estudiaba en la universidad.
No, todavía estudié en la universidad.
turns.why: What was going on in your life at that time (todavía = still) → imperfect: estudiaba.

turns.es: ¡Ah, qué padre! Entonces eran muy jóvenes.
turns.en: Oh, cool! So you were very young.

turns.es: ¿Por qué saliste tan temprano de la fiesta anoche?
turns.en: Why did you leave the party so early last night?

turns.why: How you felt at that moment (the reason) → imperfect of estar: estaba. Tiredness uses estar, not ser.

turns.en: And did you get home okay?

opts: Sí, pero mientras manejé, empezaba a llover muchísimo.
Sí, pero mientras manejo, empezó a llover muchísimo.
Sí, pero mientras manejaba, empezó a llover muchísimo.
turns.why: Mientras + action in progress (manejaba), interrupted by an event (empezó).

turns.en: Yikes! Good thing you got home safe.

¿Y a qué hora empezabas a trabajar?

turns.why: One event (moving to Chicago) → preterite, usted: vino. Viniste is tú.

turns.es: El viernes. Dijo que quería pasar más tiempo con su familia.

opts: ¡Qué sorpresa! Yo no sabía que estaba cansado del trabajo.
¡Qué sorpresa! Yo no supe que estuvo cansado del trabajo.
¡Qué sorpresa! Yo no sé que estaba cansado del trabajo.
turns.why: Both are states in the past: didn't know (sabía) and was tired (estaba).

turns.en: Nobody knew. We were all surprised.

turns.es: ¿Por qué no viniste al partido el sábado?
turns.en: Why didn't you come to the game on Saturday?

turns.why: Her condition at that time (the background reason) → imperfect of estar: estaba.

turns.en: Oh no! What did she have?

Tuvo fiebre y le duele la garganta mañana.

turns.en: Poor thing. Is she better now?

turns.why: He asks about now → present: ya está mejor.

roleplay.title: Doña Carmen's childhood
roleplay.setup: You are chatting with Doña Carmen, your elderly neighbor, on her front porch. Ask her about her childhood in Mexico and how she came to Chicago. Use usted.
roleplay.persona: You are Doña Carmen, 78, born in a small town (un pueblo) in Jalisco, Mexico. The learner is your younger neighbor; you call him 'mijo' and use tú with him, but he should use usted with you. Background: you grew up on a small ranch with seven brothers and sisters; your father grew corn and beans; every morning you carried water from the well and helped your mother make tortillas; you walked 30 minutes to the elementary school; on Sundays the whole family went to Mass and then to the plaza. You met your husband, Rogelio, at a town fiesta when you were 18; you married at 20; you came to Chicago in 1972 because Rogelio found work in a steel mill; it was January and it was the first time you saw snow (say it as 'era la primera vez que veía la nieve'). Speak at an intermediate level, mixing the imperfect (for habits and descriptions) and the preterite (for events). Keep sentences short and clear. Avoid the subjunctive and the pluperfect (había + participle). Reveal details only when the learner asks; react warmly to questions.
roleplay.opening: Ay, mijo, cuando yo era niña, la vida era muy diferente.
goals: Find out where she lived as a child and what her house was like
Ask what she used to do every day as a child
Find out how she met her husband
Ask when and why she came to Chicago and what it was like when she arrived

roleplay.title: The night everything went wrong
roleplay.setup: Your friend Gabriela had a crazy night on Friday. Get the whole story: set the scene, what happened, and how it ended. Use tú.
roleplay.persona: You are Gabriela, 32, from Tegucigalpa, Honduras, a friend of the learner; use tú. The story: on Friday night it was raining and very cold; you were at home alone making dinner and watching TV; it was about nine o'clock when suddenly the power went out (se fue la luz); you looked for a flashlight but couldn't find it (no pude encontrarla); you tried to call your sister but your phone had very little battery and it died; then you heard a noise at the door and you were very scared; it was your neighbor, Don Luis, with candles; you found out the next day that a tree fell on a power line. Use the imperfect for the scene (llovía, hacía frío, estaba sola, eran las nueve) and the preterite for events. Keep language intermediate, with short sentences. Avoid the subjunctive and the pluperfect. Tell the story only bit by bit, as the learner asks questions.
roleplay.opening: ¡No sabes lo que me pasó el viernes en la noche!
goals: Ask what the weather was like and what she was doing at home
Find out what time it was when the power went out
Find out whether she managed to call anyone
Ask who was at the door and how she found out why the power went out
